title: GPU fleet tenant shadowing and latency fences
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design and implement a tenant shadowing subsystem and runtime "latency fences" to detect and mitigate noisy-tenant interference in Dedicated GPU pools. This ticket scopes: (1) a lightweight shadowing runner that periodically mirrors small proportions of production traffic from candidate tenants to measure their contention impact in isolation; (2) an enforcement primitive (latency fence) that caps tail latency contributions per-tenant and triggers graceful degradation (rate-limit, batch-size reduction, or temporary placement) when thresholds are crossed; (3) integration with autoscaler and quota controller so corrective actions respect throughput guarantees for committed tenants and prioritized tiers.
acceptance_criteria: Shadowing runner deployed to 2 staging pools and able to mirror <5% of selected tenant traffic without affecting original request paths
Latency fence primitive exposed as a per-tenant runtime policy that can be toggled via config and enforces 95th percentile token latency budget within 10% of target
Automated action mappings: when fence is crossed, system chooses among (throttle, reduce batch, migrate to spare lane) based on tenant SLA and remaining credits
Dashboard and alerting: per-tenant contention score, fence triggers, and remediation actions visible in Console with links to sample traces
E2E regression tests that simulate a noisy model workload and validate that committed tenants retain throughput within declared guarantees while noisy tenant is throttled
tasks: Spec: define metrics, fence thresholds, and action decision matrix (owner: D. Park)
Build: implement shadowing runner and sampling hooks in ingress (owner: M. Li)
Runtime: add per-tenant fence enforcement layer to allocator loop (owner: S. Ortega)
Policy: extend quota-controller to honor fence signals and map to autoscale policies (owner: R. Chen)
Observability: wire metrics to Console, add dashboard + alert playbooks (owner: J. Singh)
Tests: chaos test that introduces a noisy-embedding job and validates fence behavior (owner: QA team)
Security/Review: run security review for shadowing data path and KMS access (owner: Security)
Rollout: gradual rollout plan + canary gating (owner: EngOps)
comments: 2025-01-12 - Aisha Kumar: Kickoff notes added. We should prioritize committed-tenants SLA protection first; shadowing targets will initially be low risk (<2% traffic).

2025-01-20 - Daniel Park: Decided to implement fence actions in order: 1) reduce batch window 2) throttle new requests 3) migrate to spare lane. Migration requires coordination with autoscaler. Added dependency on ENG-714159 for predictive throttle service.
2025-01-28 - M. Li: PoC for shadowing runner shows negligible overhead (0.6% p50 increase) in staging when sampling at 1%. Need to validate KV cache side-effects for cached prompts.
2025-01-30 - S. Ortega: Implementation note - we'll attach fence state to tenant lease metadata and check in allocator admission path; this avoids per-request RPCs.

2025-02-02 - R. Chen: Policy mapping drafted in doc: higher-tier tenants consume 'escape credits' before migration; lower-tier tenants face immediate batch reduction then throttle. See design doc link.
2025-02-03 - J. Singh: Console dashboard prototype uploaded to Grafana and linked in PR. Alert thresholds currently set at fence_trigger_count > 3 in 10m.
